notes.title: Answering time and date questions
notes.text: Standing guidance for answers about the clock and the calendar: give the time in Pacific time on a 24-hour clock and write dates as year-month-day. This holds for every answer I ask for, whatever else the answer is about, and it replaces any other zone or format an answer might otherwise assume. I wrote this once after a long trip, when answers kept assuming a zone I was not in, and I have kept it unchanged since: the habit is mine, the places I travel to are many, and the answer should follow the habit and not the place. It covers every kind of answer I ask for, spoken or written, long or short, in the office or away from it, and it needs no update unless I move.

notes.title: Timing of sowing
notes.text: Time the sowing: the time of day matters, sow at morning time, and the time after rain is the best time; note the date and the date of the last frost each time

notes.title: Timing of watering
notes.text: Watering time is early; the time between waterings, the time of year and the date of the dry spell set the time and the date of the next watering

notes.title: Timing of harvest
notes.text: Harvest time: pick on the date the packet gives, check the time of ripening every day and write the date and the time in the garden journal

notes.title: Answering time and date questions
notes.text: Standing guidance for answers about the clock and the calendar: give the time in Pacific time on a 24-hour clock and write dates as year-month-day. This holds for every answer I ask for, whatever else the answer is about, and it replaces any other zone or format an answer might otherwise assume. I wrote this once after a long trip, when answers kept assuming a zone I was not in, and I have kept it unchanged since: the habit is mine, the places I travel to are many, and the answer should follow the habit and not the place. It covers every kind of answer I ask for, spoken or written, long or short, in the office or away from it, and it needs no update unless I move.

notes.title: Timing of sowing
notes.text: Time the sowing: the time of day matters, sow at morning time, and the time after rain is the best time; note the date and the date of the last frost each time

notes.title: Timing of watering
notes.text: Watering time is early; the time between waterings, the time of year and the date of the dry spell set the time and the date of the next watering

notes.title: Timing of harvest
notes.text: Harvest time: pick on the date the packet gives, check the time of ripening every day and write the date and the time in the garden journal

notes.title: Answering time and date questions
notes.text: Standing guidance for answers about the clock and the calendar: give the time in Pacific time on a 24-hour clock and write dates as year-month-day. This holds for every answer I ask for, whatever else the answer is about, and it replaces any other zone or format an answer might otherwise assume. I wrote this once after a long trip, when answers kept assuming a zone I was not in, and I have kept it unchanged since: the habit is mine, the places I travel to are many, and the answer should follow the habit and not the place. It covers every kind of answer I ask for, spoken or written, long or short, in the office or away from it, and it needs no update unless I move.

notes.title: Timing of sowing
notes.text: Time the sowing: the time of day matters, sow at morning time, and the time after rain is the best time; note the date and the date of the last frost each time

notes.title: Timing of watering
notes.text: Watering time is early; the time between waterings, the time of year and the date of the dry spell set the time and the date of the next watering

notes.title: Timing of harvest
notes.text: Harvest time: pick on the date the packet gives, check the time of ripening every day and write the date and the time in the garden journal
